ns0:a.ns1:title: G.1 (I.cn.1): Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.
G.2 (I.def.15): A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another ;
G.3 (I.post.1): To draw a straight line from any point to any point.
G.4 (I.post.3): To describe a circle with any centre and distance.
G.5 (I.1): On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.
G.6 (I.cn.3): If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.
G.7 (I.post.2): To produce a finite straight line continuously in a straight line.
G.8 (I.2): To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.
G.9 (I.3): Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.
G.10 (I.cn.4): [7] 4. Things which coincide with one another are equal to one another.

G.16 (I.9): To bisect a given rectilineal angle.
G.17 (I.10): To bisect a given finite straight line.

G.19 (I.11): To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.
G.20 (I.12): To a given infinite straight line, from a given point which is not on it, to draw a perpendicular straight line.
G.21 (I.cn.2): If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal.
G.22 (I.13): If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.
G.23 (I.post.4): That all right angles are equal to one another.
G.25 (I.15): If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.
G.26 (I.cn.5): [8] 5. The whole is greater than the part.
G.27 (I.16): In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles.
G.28 (I.17): In any triangle two angles taken together in any manner are less than two right angles.
G.29 (I.18): In any triangle the greater side subtends the greater angle.
G.30 (I.19): In any triangle the greater angle is subtended by the greater side.
G.31 (I.20): In any triangle two sides taken together in any manner are greater than the remaining one.

G.34 (I.23): On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.

G.38 (I.def.23): Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet one another in either direction.
G.39 (I.27): If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

G.44 (I.31): Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.
G.443 (XI.1): A part of a straight line cannot be in the plane of reference and a part in a plane more elevated.
G.444 (XI.2): If two straight lines cut one another, they are in one plane, and every triangle is in one plane.
G.445 (XI.3): If two planes cut one another, their common section is a straight line.
G.446 (XI.def.3): A straight line is at right angles to a plane, when it makes right angles with all the straight lines which meet it and are in the plane.
G.447 (XI.4): If a straight line be set up at right angles to two straight lines which cut one another, at their common point of section, it will also be at right angles to the plane through the...
G.448 (XI.5): If a straight line be set up at right angles to three straight lines which meet one another, at their common point of section, the three straight lines are in one plane.
G.449 (XI.6): If two straight lines be at right angles to the same plane, the straight lines will be parallel.
G.450 (XI.7): If two straight lines be parallel and points be taken at random on each of them, the straight line joining the points is in the same plane with the parallel straight lines.
G.451 (XI.8): If two straight lines be parallel, and one of them be at right angles to any plane, the remaining one will also be at right angles to the same plane.
G.452 (XI.9): Straight lines which are parallel to the same straight line and are not in the same plane with it are also parallel to one another.
G.454 (XI.11): From a given elevated point to draw a straight line perpendicular to a given plane.
G.457 (XI.def.8): Parallel planes are those which do not meet.
G.458 (XI.14): Planes to which the same straight line is at right angles will be parallel.
G.459 (XI.15): If two straight lines meeting one another be parallel to two straight lines meeting one another, not being in the same plane, the planes through them are parallel.
